rules.description: This kernel executes 209715200 fused and 67289088 non-fused FP32 instructions. By converting pairs of non-fused instructions to their fused (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/floating-point/#cuda-and-floating-point), higher-throughput equivalent, the achieved FP32 performance could be increased by up to 12% (relative to its current performance). Check the Source page to identify where this kernel executes FP32 instructions.

rules.name: LaunchConfiguration
rules.description: A wave of thread blocks is defined as the maximum number of blocks that can be executed in parallel on the target GPU. The number of blocks in a wave depends on the number of multiprocessors and the theoretical occupancy of the kernel. This kernel launch results in 1 full waves and a partial wave of 861 thread blocks. Under the assumption of a uniform execution duration of all thread blocks, this partial wave may account for up to 50.0% of the total runtime of this kernel. Try launching a grid with no partial wave. The overall impact of this tail effect also lessens with the number of full waves executed for a grid. See the Hardware Model (https://docs.nvidia.com/nsight-compute/ProfilingGuide/index.html#metrics-hw-model) description for more details on launch configurations.

rules.name: AchievedOccupancy
rules.description: The difference between calculated theoretical (56.2%) and measured achieved occupancy (44.4%) can be the result of warp scheduling overheads or workload imbalances during the kernel execution. Load imbalances can occur between warps within a block as well as across blocks of the same kernel. See the CUDA Best Practices Guide (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-best-practices-guide/index.html#occupancy) for more details on optimizing occupancy.
